• Write the important things down several times by hand. I sometimes copied entire chapters by hand once and then it was stuck in my head.

  • Read out loud, I usually read in another language than my 1st or make a weird accent seems to get it to stick better.

Writing by hand definitely helps, more so than typing for some reason. And either of those is better than just reading it. If possible, use little diagrams and flow charts in your notes to connect ideas. Adding something more than plain text makes it more memorable and helps you visualize the connections.

Okay, so here's the official answer...

  • Be motivated to remember at the point of encoding - Be in the right mindset when studying.
  • Study for recall, not recognition - Think of recall as answering a short-answer question; think of recognition as answering a multiple choice question.
  • Distribute practice - Space out your practice/study sessions at least 1 week apart for a given topic.
  • Perform practice testing - You will learn more by studying half as much, and testing yourself for the other half of the time, even without feedback on the tests.
  • Avoid retroactive and proactive distractions - Either study when you get up, or before you go to sleep.

From everything I've seen, these techniques work. That said, I have near eidetic memory, so I rarely use any of them - I just listen to the material and it is memorized.
